usable_content: This study reports a re-analysis of plasma metabolomic data from renal cell carcinoma (RCC) patients in the CheckMate 025 trial (nivolumab vs everolimus), finding that higher baseline plasma inosine levels correlate with longer overall survival specifically in the nivolumab arm (median OS 33 months vs 22 months for high vs low groups). The authors confirm that metabolic profiling of ICB-treated human cancers supports the association between inosine levels and ICB sensitivity. Mechanistically, the study identifies that inosine directly inhibits the ubiquitin-activating enzyme UBA6 in tumor cells, enhancing tumor immunogenicity and MHC-I expression, rather than acting primarily on T cells. This provides a specific molecular link between a microbiota-associated metabolite (inosine) and tumor-intrinsic resistance to ICB.
